Hi Vanessa — appreciate the recap and the checklist. High-level answers below; I attached our compliance matrix for reference.

- PHI scoping: EU patient data (identifiers, clinical notes, device telemetry tagged as PHI) must remain exclusively in the EU. Non-PHI analytics data can be stored in US or EU.
- Retention: PHI retention is 7 years for clinical records. Backups that may contain PHI must be retained to meet that requirement (7y).
- Logs/audit: Security logs should be retained for 180 days in searchable form and archived for 7 years. Logs that contain PHI are treated as PHI.
- Failover: Our legal & ops preference is warm-standby in-region for EU customers; cross-border failover (EU -> US) would require a formal exception and only allowed for short RTOs in disaster scenarios.
- KMS: We prefer customer-managed keys for all PHI backups.

Next steps: I looped in Sven (legal) and Amira (security). They want Redwood to outline the specific configuration options (warm standby, snapshot restore cadence, encryption model) and the compliance tradeoffs. We can do the deep-dive on Wed 10 Jul at 14:00 CEST if that works for your tech folks.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Product & Partnerships
HealthMetrics Inc.

Vanessa/Monica — my recommendation (summary) and what we can commit to for a POC: see attached pinning-options-summary.pdf.

Recommendation summary:
- EU PHI: Recommend Dedicated EU-primary with warm-standby in a second EU AZ/region (depends on customer cloud preference). This satisfies EU-only residency for primary compute and live backups.
- Backups & retention: Continuous snapshotting for DBs with immutable snapshots stored in customer-controlled KMS (we can support BYOK on Dedicated/Private). Snapshot retention policy configurable to 7y for PHI.
- Logs: Access + audit logs streamed to an archival bucket (EU) with searchable retention for 180 days; archive to cold storage for 7y. We treat any logs containing PHI as PHI and keep them in-region.
- Failover behavior: Warm-standby (live replication of model cache + incremental snapshots) gives RPO ~5–15m, RTO in low minutes depending on traffic and model size. Cold restore (snapshot-based) RPO is hours; RTO can be 1–6 hours.
- Hosted option: Possible with region pinning for metadata and token-level routing, but BYOK + guaranteed in-region snapshots are limited on hosted unless we deploy a private control plane (Private). Hosted + strict BYOK is a partial gap.

POC offer: Set up a Dedicated EU-primary environment with warm standby and a 30-day retention proof-of-configuration (we'll demo failover and snapshot restore workflow). From an ops standpoint, we need an NDA amendment for BYOK details and cloud account linkage.

Elena / Sven / Amira — thanks for the quick responses and for sharing the matrix. Below is a consolidated set of answers and a proposed path forward. I included Ben and Monica for technical follow-up.

Consolidated answers (short):
- Residency: Redwood can ensure EU-only residency for PHI with a Dedicated EU-primary + warm-standby in the EU. For strict BYOK and KMS/HSM, Private deployment is recommended, but Dedicated supports BYOK for snapshots with the right contract terms.
- Backups & retention: Snapshots are configurable; we can set immutable snapshot retention to 7 years for PHI data and store keys in a customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private.
- Logs: We will keep searchable logs for 180 days in-region and archive for 7 years. Logs containing PHI will be kept in EU by configuration.
- Failover: Warm-standby provides an RPO target of 5–15 minutes and RTO in the low minutes for most model sizes. Cold snapshot restore is available as a fallback with RPO in the order of hours.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive: Wed 10 Jul at 14:00 CEST — please confirm (I see conflicts, so we moved to Thu 11 Jul 08:00 CEST if you prefer; let me know).
2) I'll share a short config brief and a POC scope doc after the deep-dive.
3) Contract ask: we'll need to capture BYOK requirements in the SOW/NDA if HealthMetrics requires HSM-level controls.

I'll attach the filled checklist and the ops summary for review. Happy to sync in whichever timezone works.
